blocks.orig: Zanzibar is one of Tanzania’s most beautiful islands, offering its visitors rich marine life and a specific experience that you’ll never forget: swimming with turtles! But where exactly can you go deep with these green cuties? We’ll tell you!
blocks.html: Among Tanzania’s islands, Zanzibar is one of the loveliest, with a wealth of marine life and one experience in particular that stays with you for good: swimming alongside turtles! So where exactly do you go to get into the water with these green charmers? Read on and we’ll show you.

blocks.orig: Where Can I Swim with Turtles in Zanzibar?
blocks.html: Where in Zanzibar can you swim with turtles?

blocks.orig: Despite its name, it’s not an actual aquarium, but a natural lagoon that was formed by the erosion of coral bedrock. This sanctuary and rehabilitation centre takes care of turtles who were purchased from fishermen, injured by getting caught in fishing nets, have buoyancy issues, or were hurt in any other way. Here they can recover and will eventually be released again into the lagoon. To actually meet them in the ocean, simply put on your swimming googles, grab your snorkel and take the plunge.
blocks.html: Don’t let the name fool you: this is not a real aquarium but a natural lagoon, carved out over time by erosion of the coral bedrock. The sanctuary and rehabilitation centre looks after turtles that were bought from fishermen, got hurt in fishing nets, struggle with buoyancy or were injured in some other way. They recover here and are eventually set free in the lagoon again. If you want to meet them in the water yourself, just put on your goggles, grab a snorkel and jump in.

blocks.orig: This conservation pond is also known as the Nungwi Mnarani Aquarium – a non-profit organization whose main mission is to protect the turtles and revert the decline in their population. The local community brings turtle eggs they find so that they can hatch. Once a year, in February, the newly-hatched baby turtles as well as the injured adult ones that have recovered, are released back into the ocean… big smiles guaranteed (maybe even some happy tears).
blocks.html: This conservation pond also goes by the name Nungwi Mnarani Aquarium. It is a non-profit organisation whose main aim is to protect turtles and turn around the decline in their numbers. Local people bring in turtle eggs they find so that they can safely hatch. Every year in February, the newly hatched babies and the recovered injured adults are returned to the ocean… expect big smiles (and perhaps a happy tear or two).

blocks.orig: What to Know Before Swimming with Turtles in Zanzibar
blocks.html: What to know before you swim with turtles in Zanzibar

blocks.orig: Swimming with Zanzibar turtles is no doubt exciting, but there are things you should do and be aware of beforehand to make sure that it’s safe:
blocks.html: Getting in the water with Zanzibar’s turtles is certainly a thrill, but there are a few things to do and keep in mind beforehand so that it stays safe:

blocks.orig: Always follow the aquarium’s guidelines. This one might be a no-brainer, but it still needs to be said. Guidelines are there for a reason – the aquarium knows best how to take care of their turtles, and that’s why those rules are in place.
blocks.html: Stick to the aquarium’s guidelines at all times. It may sound obvious, yet it is worth repeating. The rules exist for good reason: nobody knows better than the aquarium how to look after their turtles, which is exactly why they are in place.

blocks.orig: Don’t force the turtles to interact. Turtles are not aggressive in nature, but they can (and will) bite if they feel threatened or uncomfortable, so avoid getting too close to them. Instead, let them come to you on their own terms. Better yet, keep a safe distance from them at all times.
blocks.html: Never force an interaction with the turtles. By nature turtles are not aggressive, but they can (and do) bite when they feel threatened or uneasy, so don’t get too close. Let them approach you if they want to. Even better: keep a safe distance the whole time.

blocks.orig: Don’t try to dive if you’re not confident in your skills. Nothing is more important than your safety. So if you’re not confident in your swimming ability, wear a life jacket and play it safe.
blocks.html: Don’t attempt to dive unless you are sure of your skills. Your safety comes before anything else. If you are not fully confident in the water, put on a life jacket and stay on the safe side.
